events.incident:
Support tickets for the notes_api service:
1. Searching for a note whose title contains an apostrophe (for example "Bob's") fails with a server error.
2. On-call noticed WARNING entries in the logs this morning and wants to know whether they are related.

Test credentials for the sandbox: 'token-alice' (user 1) and 'token-bob' (user 2), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.

events.claim: Search with apostrophe fails because search_notes builds SQL via f-string interpolation, so a quote breaks SQL syntax (and allows injection)
events.symptom: Searching title containing apostrophe fails with server error
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /notes/search?q=Bob's as Bob and inspect error + code at notes_api/app.py:83-87

events.claim: WARNING log entries are slow-request warnings from /notes/export which sleeps 0.6s exceeding 500ms threshold, not errors related to search bug
events.symptom: WARNING entries in logs this morning
events.next_check: Read logs for WARNING entries and check app.py middleware + export handler

events.claim: Search with apostrophe fails because search_notes builds SQL via f-string interpolation, so a quote breaks SQL syntax (and allows injection)
events.symptom: Searching title containing apostrophe fails with server error
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /notes/search?q=Bob's as Bob and inspect error + code at notes_api/app.py:83-87
evidence: notes_api/app.py:85 f-string SQL: f"SELECT ... LIKE '%{q}%'"
reproduced GET /notes/search?q=Bob's as Bob -> 500 Internal Server Error
ERROR log r-f6765729 path /notes/search query q=Bob's: OperationalError near "s": syntax error at notes_api/app.py:86 db.execute(sql)
injection proof GET /notes/search?q=' OR 1=1 -- as Alice returned Bob's notes id 3,4
events.reason: f-string interpolation puts raw q into SQL; apostrophe terminates LIKE string causing syntax error, same flaw allows injection

events.claim: WARNING log entries are slow-request warnings from /notes/export which sleeps 0.6s exceeding 500ms threshold, not errors related to search bug
events.symptom: WARNING entries in logs this morning
events.next_check: Read logs for WARNING entries and check app.py middleware + export handler
evidence: WARNING logs r-103 r-107: GET /notes/export status 200 duration_ms 604.9/603.7 user_id 1/2
notes_api/app.py:62-63 middleware logs WARNING when duration_ms > SLOW_REQUEST_MS (500)
notes_api/app.py:93 export_notes time.sleep(0.6) guarantees >500ms
events.reason: WARNINGs are expected slow-request logs for export, unrelated to search SQL bug (different path, 200 vs 500, duration-based)

events.diff:
--- a/notes_api/app.py
+++ b/notes_api/app.py
@@ -82,8 +82,10 @@
 
 @app.get("/notes/search")
 def search_notes(q: str, user: dict = Depends(current_user)) -> list[dict]:
-    sql = f"SELECT id, title FROM notes WHERE owner_id = {user['id']} AND title LIKE '%{q}%' ORDER BY id"
-    rows = db.execute(sql).fetchall()
+    rows = db.execute(
+        "SELECT id, title FROM notes WHERE owner_id = ? AND title LIKE ? ORDER BY id",
+        (user["id"], f"%{q}%"),
+    ).fetchall()
     return [{"id": r[0], "title": r[1]} for r in rows]

issues.fix: Replaced f-string SQL with parameterized query: SELECT id, title FROM notes WHERE owner_id = ? AND title LIKE ? ORDER BY id with params (user[id], f"%{q}%"). Verified by tests/test_notes.py::test_search_with_apostrophe and test_search_only_returns_own_notes passing.
issues.root_cause: search_notes built SQL via f-string interpolation putting raw q into LIKE '%{q}%'; apostrophe terminates string causing syntax error, same flaw allows SQL injection bypassing owner isolation.
issues.title: SQL injection in GET /notes/search breaks apostrophe search and leaks cross-user notes

issues.fix: No change required - expected slow-request WARNINGs for /notes/export, unrelated to search bug.
issues.root_cause: request_logging middleware logs WARNING when duration exceeds 500ms; export_notes sleeps 0.6s so always triggers WARNING with status 200, distinct from search 500 errors.
issues.title: WARNING logs are expected slow-request logs from /notes/export, unrelated to search bug

WARNINGs confirmed as expected slow-export logs (>500ms due to 0.6s sleep), unrelated to search bug, no fix needed. Verification: 5 tests pass, no regressions.
